relations.name: SUPPORTS
glosses: A supports B when A provides evidence that makes B more credible.
The source endpoint is the evidence or reason; the target endpoint is the claim or conclusion being supported.
Support is evidential strengthening, not correction, replacement, provenance, causation, or simple chronology.

relations.name: CORRECTS
glosses: A corrects B when A fixes an error or inaccurate detail in B.
The source endpoint carries the correction; the target endpoint is the record or statement containing the error.
Correction changes an erroneous claim without meaning that A merely replaces B as the current authority.

relations.name: SUPERSEDES
glosses: A supersedes B when A replaces B as the version or authority that should now govern.
The source endpoint is the replacement or newer authority; the target endpoint is the displaced older version.
Supersession is about precedence and replacement, not merely happening later in time.

relations.name: DERIVED_FROM
glosses: A is derived from B when A was produced, computed, summarized, or otherwise created using B as its source material.
The source endpoint is the derived artifact; the target endpoint is the provenance base it came from.
Derivation expresses provenance, not evidential support or causal production of an event.

relations.name: CAUSES
glosses: A causes B when the condition or event in A brings about the event or outcome in B.
The source endpoint is the cause or antecedent; the target endpoint is the consequence.
Causation is stronger than evidence that merely supports a claim and stronger than temporal succession alone.

relations.name: TEMPORAL_SUCCESSOR
glosses: A is the temporal successor of B when A comes after B in the relevant chronology.
The source endpoint is the later record or event; the target endpoint is its earlier predecessor.
Temporal succession encodes ordering in time without by itself implying replacement, correction, or causation.
